gap: No result ChatGPT got states that no 2,000 Wh-class station is under $600 on its maker's own US store today (cheapest: AFERIY P210 at $602.10, FOSSiBOT F2400 at $669), so the only sub-$600 prices are Amazon listings (FOSSiBOT $599.00, DYNESS $539.99) and third-party deals, with Jackery's own Explorer 2000 v2 price at $999, $416.06 above the deal ChatGPT showed.
standout_why: I could not open any rival page: WebFetch failed on every URL with a TLS error and curl was blocked, so the 2 is inferred, not read. It rests on the result titles (cheapestwh.com and outletpicks.com present themselves as Amazon and outlet cost-per-Wh trackers) and on ChatGPT's answer, which repeats tracker and deal-seller prices and tells the shopper to verify the seller. On that evidence they lack the maker-store price beside each deal price, the list of big-brand models that miss the cap and by how much, and the AFERIY P210's $2.10 miss. If outletpicks or cheapestwh do print maker-store prices, this drops to 1.
decides: It confirms the FOSSiBOT F2400 as the pick, but only at Amazon's $599.00, which is $70 under FOSSiBOT's own store ($669); FOSSiBOT's store states a 5-year full-device warranty. DYNESS at $539.99 on Amazon is the cheapest listing I could verify. The Jackery deal at $582.94 sits $416.06 below Jackery's own pre-order price, so it is a seller-risk buy, not a like-for-like price. Every established-brand 2 kWh unit I priced starts at $879 or more (the smaller-output Anker S2000 is $699.99 on Amazon), and none of Dealectric's listed 2 kWh products qualifies (Growatt $799, BLUETTI $899). One constraint for the page: the amzcheck tool's own notes say our pages never print an Amazon price (DLC-159), so the two sub-$600 figures may need to be described rather than printed.

Anker SOLIX F2000 price at ankersolix.com and the legitimacy of the $599 coupon WSTD8XPDN1 deal: storecheck.py returned HTTP 404 on both search and the product URL. A search snippet mentioned a $749 Anker Outlet eBay price, which I did not open and so do not report as a finding.
DYNESS warranty length, weight and a maker's US store price: I found no DYNESS consumer store to query, and amzcheck returns only title, price and rating.
ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 (1,920 Wh) price today: allpowers.com returned a non-JSON response to storecheck twice (www) and HTTP 404 on the bare domain.
Segway Cube 2000 price today: store.segway.com returned HTTP 404 to storecheck; the $539 Amazon price in the Electrek title dates from 2026-02-23 and was not opened.
FOSSiBOT F2400 weight (ChatGPT says 48.5 lb): the product-page call returned HTTP 429 and the search text does not give a weight.

Amazon rating counts: amzcheck returned the same count (368) for the FOSSiBOT and DYNESS listings and the same count (755) for two different Anker listings, so I treated the rating fields as unreliable and left them out.
Third-party deal prices ChatGPT or its results showed (Jackery $582.94, ECO-WORTHY $516 and $557.18, AFERIY $599.99 low on deal.ai): none of those pages could be opened.
